page: Microsoft Azure D16ps_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the arm64 architecture, powered by 16 physical cores of an ARM Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz. The instance implements a dedicated core model with one thread per core, backed by 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and 128 MB of shared L3 cache. It provides 64 GB of RAM, equating to an even 4 GB per virtual core. The instance includes no bundled local storage disks and no graphics hardware accelerators, utilizing Microsoft Hyper-V to manage host virtualization.

Benchmark evaluations reveal distinct subsystem traits, most notably within memory access. In the PassMark memory evaluation, the platform ranks in the top 10 percent, supported by uncached large-block read transfers reaching 300.63 GB/sec and write transfers reaching 111.74 GB/sec. Single-threaded gzip compression also falls into the top 25 percent at 33.12 GB/sec. Standard computational workloads deliver median results, with Geekbench multi-core scoring 14440.0 and stress-ng yielding 33154.29. Natural language processing models without GPU acceleration reflect slower execution, with prompt processing on a 7B parameter model ranking in the lower quartile at 24.67 tokens per second.

Because the D16ps_v6 does not provision local NVMe or ephemeral storage, all persistent and scratch filesystem operations require external storage volumes. This trade-off emphasizes compute predictability and memory bandwidth over low-latency local disk access. The architecture offers strong resource efficiency for infrastructure environments where workloads do not rely on x86-specific vector extensions such as AVX-512.

Workload fit covers general cloud-native applications requiring uniform core performance without hyperthreaded contention. The system is well matched to in-memory caching platforms such as Redis, web application tiers, static web serving, containerized microservices, and continuous integration environments running software compilation under Clang.
description: Microsoft Azure D16ps_v6 is an arm64 general-purpose virtual machine featuring 16 physical ARM Neoverse-N2 cores clocked at 3.4 GHz with one thread per core and 64 GB of system memory. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, the system incorporates 128 MB of L3 cache and maintains a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It excludes local storage and GPU hardware, relying on external network volumes for persistent data. Benchmark metrics show top-tier memory performance, achieving over 300 GB/sec in large-block uncached read bandwidth and scoring within the upper 10 percent in PassMark memory tests, alongside upper-quartile single-threaded gzip throughput. General CPU execution across Geekbench and stress-ng reflects steady mid-tier capability, while 7B model prompt processing reveals limitations for CPU-based deep learning. The server is well configured for in-memory databases, Redis deployments, software compilation, web serving, and containerized cloud application tiers.
